source_text: Urban sensing platforms are increasingly used to monitor traffic conditions in real time. These platforms collect traffic observations continuously from roadside devices. Continuous traffic observations can support faster identification of congestion. In this study, the platform is evaluated only for arterial roads during weekday peak periods.
protected_challenge: Remove repeated wording without deleting a distinct claim
content_units: urban sensing platforms monitor traffic in real time
evaluation restricted to arterial roads and weekday peaks

source_text: Smart waste collection is an important and promising approach for modern cities. Many systems can improve waste services in useful ways. The present study evaluates a routing controller that receives bin fill estimates every 15 minutes and dispatches two collection vehicles in a synthetic district. The study measures travel distance and missed-overflow events.
protected_challenge: Improve specificity using only supplied facts; no new novelty claim
content_units: routing controller receives fill estimates every 15 minutes
measures travel distance and missed-overflow events

source_text: Study A reported lower latency after edge aggregation, whereas Study B observed no latency reduction under sparse traffic. Study C focused on energy consumption and reported a 12% decrease when messages were batched. Study D found that batching increased delay during emergency bursts. Together, these studies examine different operating conditions and should not be summarized as a single consistent effect.
protected_challenge: Distinguish multiple studies and contrasting findings
content_units: Study A lower latency after edge aggregation
Study B no latency reduction under sparse traffic
Study C 12% energy decrease with batching
Study D batching increased delay during emergency bursts

source_text: Adaptive signal timing reduced mean queue length in the simulated corridor [CIT_SYN_01]. A separate experiment found that packet loss increased when roadside-unit density was reduced [CIT_SYN_02]. These findings concern different subsystems and should not be treated as evidence for the same mechanism.
protected_challenge: Keep each citation linked to same supported claim
content_units: CIT_SYN_01 supports reduced mean queue length
CIT_SYN_02 supports increased packet loss with reduced RSU density

source_text: Among vehicles observed during the evening window, higher beacon density was associated with shorter discovery time. The result may reflect improved neighbor awareness, but the experiment does not establish that beacon density causes the reduction. The finding was not evaluated outside the evening window.
protected_challenge: Preserve uncertainty, population restriction and negation
content_units: association higher beacon density and shorter discovery time

source_text: At 08:00, Group A required 42.0 s to complete the route, compared with 51.5 s for Group B. At 14:00, Group A required 46.2 s, while Group B required 49.8 s. Relative to the 08:00 baseline, Group A therefore increased by 4.2 s.

The controller first discards readings older than 60 s. It then normalizes valid sensor values using parameters fixed before evaluation. Vehicles with missing position data are excluded from route optimization. The optimizer runs for 200 iterations with seed 17, after which the selected route is stored without further tuning.
protected_challenge: Preserve ordered steps, conditions, exclusions and reproducibility details
content_units: discard readings older than 60 s first
normalize valid values using pre-fixed parameters

source_text: Across the tested scenarios, lower channel occupancy was associated with higher delivery ratio. This pattern was strongest in medium-density traffic. Because the experiment did not manipulate channel occupancy independently, the result does not demonstrate that reducing occupancy will cause higher delivery ratio in other networks.
protected_challenge: Association must not become causation or broader generalization
content_units: association lower channel occupancy with higher delivery ratio

source_text: The scheduler calculates the priority value P_i = w_1U_i + w_2D_i for every task i. U_i is utilization and D_i is normalized deadline pressure. The weights w_1 and w_2 are fixed before the run. A task obtains a larger priority only when the weighted combination becomes larger; the equation itself is not changed during adaptation.
protected_challenge: Preserve technical terms, symbols/equation identity and explanation

source_text: It is important to emphasize that the proposed monitoring procedure provides a structured mechanism for collecting measurements in a consistent manner. In particular, the procedure collects one measurement every 30 s from each active node, and it stores the timestamp and node identifier with every measurement. This structured and consistent collection mechanism is important because the subsequent analysis groups measurements by node and by five-minute interval. No imputation is performed for missing measurements.
protected_challenge: Remove empty repetition without compression of required information
content_units: one measurement every 30 s from each active node
analysis groups by node and five-minute interval

source_text: The gateway receives each report. The gateway checks the report identifier. The gateway checks the report timestamp. The gateway rejects duplicate reports. The gateway forwards accepted reports to the storage service. The storage service records the original timestamp.
protected_challenge: Improve rhythm where useful without arbitrary variation

source_text: The evaluation includes three traffic densities. Reliability is measured as delivery ratio. Delay is also measured. The controller uses the same parameter values in all densities. The purpose of keeping the parameters fixed is to determine whether performance changes arise under different loads rather than from retuning the controller.
protected_challenge: Strengthen argument progression with justified local reorder/split/merge
content_units: fixed parameters isolate load effects from retuning
